::: {#exr-reversed-text-entropy}
#### Predicting a text backward

A reader can guess a text one character at a time from its start,
guessing each character from the characters already read.
The reader can also guess it from its end,
guessing each character from the characters that follow it.
Most people find the backward game harder,
so does a reversed text carry more information per character than the text read forward
[@mackay2003information, exercise 8.11]?

Model the text as a [stationary sequence](#def-stationary-sequence) $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ of characters
that is also an [$N$-gram model](#def-n-gram-model) with $N \ge 2$,
and let $n \ge N$.

1. Use the [chain rule for entropy](#thm-entropy-chain-rule-n), with the variables listed in each of two orders, to show that

   $$
   \sum_{t=1}^{n} \entropyf{X_t \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{t-1}}
   = \sum_{t=1}^{n} \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t+1}, \ldots, X_n},
   $$

   where the term for $t = 1$ on the left and the term for $t = n$ on the right are unconditional [entropies](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy).

2. For $N < t \le n$, show that the forward [conditional entropy](#def-conditional-entropy) of $X_t$ is

   $$
   \entropyf{X_t \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{t-1}}
   = \entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_N} - \entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_{N-1}}.
   $$

3. For $1 \le t \le n - N + 1$, show that given all the later characters,
   $X_t$ depends only on the $N - 1$ characters just after it:
   for every choice of values $x_t, \ldots, x_n$ with $\P(X_{t+1} = x_{t+1}, \ldots, X_n = x_n) > 0$,

   $$
   \P(X_t = x_t \mid X_{t+1} = x_{t+1}, \ldots, X_n = x_n)
   = \P(X_t = x_t \mid X_{t+1} = x_{t+1}, \ldots, X_{t+N-1} = x_{t+N-1}).
   $$

4. For $1 \le t \le n - N + 1$, show that the backward conditional entropy of $X_t$ is

   $$
   \entropyf{X_t \mid X_{t+1}, \ldots, X_n}
   = \entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_N} - \entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_{N-1}}.
   $$

   What do parts 1, 2 and 4 say about the two guessing games?

:::
